title: Conditional stopPropagation — only swallow when inner actually handled
trigger: Nested event handlers (inner + outer) where the inner handler only handles a subset of cases
principle: `stopPropagation` is a "swallow event" — only call it when the handler actually consumes the event. When an inner handler returns early because its case doesn't match (external drop when inner only handles internal reorder, click outside when inner only handles click-inside), the event must be allowed to bubble to the outer handler. Unconditional `stopPropagation` at the top of a function is a silent dead path for every case the inner handler doesn't handle — the outer handler never runs for those cases. Pattern: check the handle condition first, `stopPropagation` after (and only when it matches).

cases.context: Nested drop handlers — inner handles internal reorder, outer handles external file drop; inner swallows the event unconditionally before checking its case

applyFor: Nested drop handlers (internal reorder + external file add) — stopPropagation only when internal drag active
Nested click handlers (popover inside dialog — stopPropagation only when click inside popover, let outside-click close dialog)
Event delegation layers (inner listener + outer listener same event type) — inner only swallows when it handles, not when it returns early
React synthetic event bubbling where outer container needs to receive the event for some cases
